metadata.register: Professional, polite, simple -- a real progress update, not overhyped, per the user's explicit tone request.
metadata.note: A CLI-explainer weekly recap -- a NEW week's log, separate from the earlier recaps (weekly-recap-foundation-search and before). Same story spine as those builds (B00 cold open -> problem -> ask -> code -> output -> change -> code -> output -> lesson -> handoff -> outro; real code shown via ClaudeCodeBeat; one required revision cycle). weekly_recap_v1.py and weekly_recap_v2.py are genuine Python scripts, both actually run; v1 is a flat list of four parts, v2 adds a STATUS to each (published / produced / saved / planning) and prints a done-vs-planning count ('3 parts done, 1 in planning') -- chosen because the user asked for an honest update and the CatBot and DogBot work is a plan, not a built tool. THE CATBOT AND DOGBOT PART is an EARLY-STAGE PLAN (user instruction): it never says the demo is built and never says any shelter has agreed to take part; the section is labelled 'Early-stage plan' on screen; the next steps are stated as plans ('the team plans to build the demo, then reach out ... aiming for one pilot shelter in each region'). ILLUSTRATED VISUALS ONLY (user instruction): a friendly illustrated cat and dog, a generic map panel for Minnesota and the Boston area with one pin each; no photos of real animals, shelters or people. NO real platform logos: the Substack article is a mock header (text kicker only), GitHub is a generic code-folder icon with a plain-text label. Video count: the user's kickoff says 'four video files ... covering two videos'; this recap uses that wording (two videos, four files). Disclosed substitutions carried forward: (1) af_bella + @HumanitariansAI instead of the skill's default voice/handle; (2) rendered through run.sh/compile.py/static_scene_check.py/manim_layout_audit.py/final_frame_check.py. Self-intro ('Hi, I'm Agrima') opens B00's narration per the user's kickoff. All items are the user's own self-reported account. The 'pushed my files to GitHub' claim is the user's statement; this toolkit session had not pushed this week's files when the video was built. No footage exists -- every visual is a generated Manim graphic.

props.code:
WEEK = [
    {"part": "1. Writing",
     "item": "Published a new Substack article: 'Real Art, New Light'"},
    {"part": "2. Video production",
     "item": "Two Brutalist videos (AI topic + weekly recap), each in 16:9 and 9:16: four files"},
    {"part": "3. Organizing the work",
     "item": "Pushed my files to GitHub"},
    {"part": "4. A new project",
     "item": "Went through the CatBot and DogBot proposal at Humanitarians AI"},
]


def log():
    for entry in WEEK:
        print(f"- {entry['part']}: {entry['item']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    log()

props.title: weekly_recap_v2.py
props.code:
WEEK = [
    {"status": "published", "part": "1. Writing",
     "item": "Substack article: 'Real Art, New Light'"},
    {"status": "produced", "part": "2. Video production",
     "item": "Two Brutalist videos, each in 16:9 and 9:16: four files"},
    {"status": "saved", "part": "3. Organizing the work",
     "item": "Files on GitHub"},
    {"status": "planning", "part": "4. A new project",
     "item": "CatBot and DogBot: an early-stage plan"},
]


def log():
    for entry in WEEK:
        print(f"[{entry['status'].upper()}] {entry['part']}: {entry['item']}")
    planning = [e for e in WEEK if e["status"] == "planning"]
    print(f"{len(WEEK) - len(planning)} parts done, {len(planning)} in planning")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    log()

beats.narration_text: Re-run it, and the picture is clear. Three parts done: the article, the videos, and the files. One part is in planning: CatBot and DogBot, an early-stage plan.
